_meta.title: Coffee-map city stats facts
_meta.units: population = persons; area_km2 = land area in square kilometres
_meta.caveat: shops_published figures come from directories with different category definitions and are NOT comparable to each other or to the project's own counts (shops_ours). See research/city-stats-dossier.md.

cities.name: Tijuana
cities.population_definition: Municipio de Tijuana (INEGI Censo 2020). City proper = localidad Tijuana, 1,810,645 (same census).
cities.area_definition: Municipio boundary, 1,239.49 km2 (IMPLAN Tijuana citing Programa Estatal de Desarrollo Urbano BC 2009-2013)
cities.shops_source: mexicocafes.com, https://mexicocafes.com/cafes/baja-california/tijuana.html (2026 directory built from economic-census 'cafeterias'; broad category incl. soda fountains/ice-cream)
cities.notes: Area in config (1,239.6) is right. Published 1,470 is ~2.3x our 627; the census category is broader than 'coffee shop'. Specialty scene is small but real (Ilustre, Infuso, BOGESCA, Magul). Cross-border foot traffic makes resident-based per-capita a weak proxy for demand.

cities.name: San Diego
cities.population_definition: City proper (Census place), Vintage 2025 estimate for July 1, 2025. 2020 census: 1,386,932.
cities.area_definition: Land area, 2024 Census Gazetteer (326.09 sq mi); excludes 120.0 km2 water
cities.notes: City boundary runs to 844.6 km2 of mostly low-density land, so municipal density undersells the walkable core. Clever (2024) ranks SD 3rd nationally at 20.8 coffee shops per 100k, but its implied absolute count only reconciles at metro scale.
cities.metro_source: Census CBSA 2024 estimate, San Diego-Chula Vista-Carlsbad

cities.name: Los Angeles
cities.population_definition: City proper (Census place), Vintage 2025 estimate. 2020 census: 3,898,747.
cities.area_definition: Land area, 2024 Census Gazetteer (470.52 sq mi)
cities.shops_source: Rentech Digital (Apr 1 2026). Other published counts for the same city: 1,890 (SavorCity), 1,733 (LocalStitch), 1,151 (Pulled, specialty-leaning)
cities.notes: The widest spread of any city here: 1,151-4,750 for the same boundary, a 4x range driven purely by category definition. Our 1,170 is at the low end. Treat LA's per-capita figure as extraction-limited, not market-limited.
cities.metro_source: Census CBSA 2024 estimate, Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim

cities.name: Mexico City
cities.population_definition: Entidad (all 16 alcaldias) = city proper, INEGI Censo 2020
cities.area_definition: Entidad, 1,485.2 km2 (INEGI, Panorama sociodemografico CDMX, EIC 2025)
cities.notes: Published 7,287 vs our 1,051 (14%) is the largest absolute gap and suggests our extraction covers only the specialty/brunch segment. Density of 6,201/km2 makes CDMX the densest city in the set by far, so per-km2 comparisons reward it despite weak extraction.
cities.metro_source: INEGI Censo 2020, ZM Valle de Mexico (76 municipios)

cities.name: Guadalajara
cities.population_definition: Municipio de Guadalajara, INEGI Censo 2020 (fully urbanised; localidad = municipio)
cities.area_definition: Municipio, 150.36 km2 (IIEG, Guadalajara diagnostico municipal, Nov 2025)
cities.notes: Config area 151.5 is close but should be 150.36. The published 1,471 vs our 201 (14%) is the biggest relative gap after CDMX: Guadalajara's cafe culture is heavily traditional (cafeterias, neverias), which our Google-Maps queries under-sample.

cities.name: Ensenada
cities.population_definition: Municipio de Ensenada after the 2020 San Quintin split, INEGI Censo 2020. City proper (localidad Ensenada): 330,652.
cities.area_definition: Municipio excluding islands, 13,313.7 km2 (INEGI figure cited in COPLADEM, Plan Municipal de Desarrollo 2025-2027)
cities.notes: Config area 14,899 km2 is stale: it predates the creation of San Quintin (2020) and San Felipe (2021) municipios. Correct current area is 13,313.7 km2. Even so, municipal density is meaningless here (27 cafes / 13,314 km2); the city itself has 330,652 people and the cafes sit almost entirely in the urban strip.
cities.metro_source: No metropolitan area defined by INEGI

cities.name: New York City
cities.population_definition: City proper (5 boroughs), Vintage 2025 estimate. 2020 census: 8,804,190.
cities.area_definition: Land area, 2024 Census Gazetteer (300.46 sq mi); excludes 445.4 km2 water
cities.notes: Highest extraction ratio of the big cities (67%), consistent with the project's NYC-heavy query set. Population density 11,031/km2 is the highest in the set, so NYC wins per-km2 metrics and sits mid-table per-capita.
cities.metro_source: Census CBSA 2024 estimate, New York-Newark-Jersey City

cities.name: Austin
cities.population_definition: City proper (Census place), Vintage 2025 estimate. 2020 census: 961,855.
cities.area_definition: Land area, 2024 Census Gazetteer (326.39 sq mi)
cities.notes: Config area 823.4 is stale; the 2024 Gazetteer gives 845.3 km2. Austin's 845 km2 boundary makes municipal density (0.38 cafes/km2) look rural while its core is dense - the clearest case for a fixed-radius metric.
cities.metro_source: Census CBSA 2024 estimate, Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos

cities.name: Seattle
cities.population_definition: City proper (Census place), Vintage 2025 estimate. 2020 census: 737,015.
cities.area_definition: Land area, 2024 Census Gazetteer (84.00 sq mi); excludes 150.4 km2 water
cities.notes: Our 773 vs 804 published = 96%, by far the best coverage match, which makes Seattle's #1 per-capita rank the most trustworthy single figure on the tab. Also note the 2011 NPD figure of 1,640 shops was metro-wide and is still quoted in local press.

cities.name: San Francisco
cities.area_definition: Land area, 2024 Census Gazetteer (46.69 sq mi); excludes 479.7 km2 water
cities.shops_source: Rentech Digital (Apr 1 2026); 627 'independent' (joe.coffee); 528 in an older study quoted by Time Out (2024)
cities.notes: Tiny, fully built-out boundary (120.9 km2) makes SF the fairest per-km2 comparison in the set. Population has fallen ~5% since 2020, which mechanically lifts any per-resident metric.

cities.name: Oakland
cities.population_definition: City proper (Census place), Vintage 2025 estimate. 2020 census: 440,646.
cities.area_definition: Land area, 2024 Census Gazetteer (55.96 sq mi); excludes 57.2 km2 water
cities.shops_source: joe.coffee, 'independent coffee shops' only (2026); Crema tracks 135 independent shops
cities.notes: The only city where our count exceeds the published figure (385 vs 164), because the only readily available Oakland count excludes chains. Not comparable to the other rows - do not rank Oakland's per-capita figure against cities with all-shop counts.
cities.metro_source: Census CBSA 2024 estimate, SF-Oakland-Fremont (Oakland has no separate MSA)
